treks.title: Kedarkantha
treks.overview: A classic first winter trek. The trail climbs through pine and oak forest, passes a frozen lake and ends on a snow-covered summit above Sankri with wide views of Swargarohini and Bandarpoonch.
itinerary: Juda ka Talab to Kedarkantha Base

treks.title: Dayara Bugyal
treks.overview: A gentle climb from Barsu to one of Uttarakhand's largest high-altitude meadows. Green in summer and under deep snow in winter, with Bandarpoonch and Srikanth in the distance.
treks.best_months: Mar to May, Oct to Nov
itinerary: Explore Bakaria Top and return to camp
treks.themes: Meadow, Family with kids, Beginner, Snow

treks.title: Brahmatal
treks.overview: A winter trek through oak and rhododendron forest to frozen lakes and a ridge that looks across to Trishul and Nanda Ghunti.
treks.themes: Snow, Lakes, Frozen River and Waterfall

treks.title: Valley of Flowers
treks.overview: A protected alpine valley covered in wildflowers in the monsoon, combined with the high-altitude shrine of Hemkund Sahib.
itinerary: Ghangaria to Valley of Flowers and back
Ghangaria to Hemkund Sahib and back
Ghangaria to Govindghat, drive to Joshimath
treks.themes: Walk in the Valley, Meadow, River

treks.title: Roopkund
treks.overview: A high trek through Ali and Bedni Bugyal meadows to a glacial lake in a stark bowl of rock, with Trishul and Nanda Ghunti in view.
treks.best_months: May to Jun, Sep to Oct

treks.title: Hampta Pass
treks.overview: A crossover trek that climbs from the green Kullu valley over Hampta Pass into the dry, rugged landscape of Lahaul, ending at Chandratal lake.
highlights: Green valley to cold desert crossover
itinerary: Manali to Jobra, trek to Chika
Balu ka Ghera to Shea Goru over Hampta Pass
Drive from Shea Goru to Chandratal

treks.title: Kashmir Great Lakes
treks.overview: A high-altitude route linking Vishansar, Krishansar, Gadsar, Satsar and Gangabal lakes between Sonamarg and Naranag, over open meadows and passes.
highlights: Meadows full of wildflowers in season
itinerary: Nichnai to Vishansar Lake via Krishansar
Vishansar to Gadsar over Gadsar Pass

treks.title: Markha Valley
treks.overview: A river-valley trek through Ladakhi villages, monasteries and apricot fields, with the Kongmaru La crossing as the high point.
itinerary: Nimaling to Kongmaru La to Chokdo
Chokdo to Hemis, drive to Leh
treks.themes: Walk in the Valley, River, Off Beat Trek

treks.title: Sandakphu
treks.overview: A walk along the Singalila ridge to the highest point in West Bengal, with a view of Everest, Kanchenjunga, Lhotse and Makalu on clear days.
highlights: Four of the five highest peaks in view
Sunrise on the Sleeping Buddha range
treks.best_months: Mar to May, Oct to Nov
itinerary: NJP to Manebhanjan, trek to Chitrey

treks.title: Goechala
treks.overview: A long trek in Kanchenjunga National Park from Yuksom through rhododendron forest and high meadows to Goechala viewpoint, passing Samiti Lake.
treks.best_months: Apr to May, Oct to Nov
itinerary: Thansing to Lamuney via Samiti Lake

treks.title: Annapurna Base Camp
treks.overview: A teahouse trek into the Annapurna Sanctuary, a high basin ringed by Annapurna I, Machapuchare and Hiunchuli.
treks.best_months: Mar to May, Oct to Nov
itinerary: Drive to Nayapul, trek to Ghandruk
Bamboo to Jhinu, drive to Pokhara

treks.title: Everest Base Camp
treks.short_text: Classic route to Everest base camp
treks.overview: The classic Khumbu trek through Sherpa villages and Sagarmatha National Park to Everest Base Camp and the Kala Patthar viewpoint.
highlights: Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar
Views of Ama Dablam, Lhotse and Nuptse
treks.best_months: Mar to May, Oct to Nov
itinerary: Fly to Lukla, trek to Phakding
Lobuche to Gorakshep and Everest Base Camp

treks.title: Chandratal Lake
treks.overview: A short, scenic trek to the crescent-shaped Chandratal lake in the Spiti region, set in a wide valley of bare mountains.
itinerary: Rest and explore around the lake
treks.themes: Lakes, Beginner, Couples, Family with kids
treks.experiences: Family Treks, Stargazing Treks, Summer Camps

treks.title: Kedarnath Trek
treks.overview: A pilgrim trail from Gaurikund to the Kedarnath temple, set at the foot of snow-capped peaks. The route is about 16 km each way.
treks.best_months: May to Jun, Sep to Oct
itinerary: Drive to Gaurikund, trek to Kedarnath

inclusions: Stay at camps, guesthouses or teahouses as per the route
Trek leader, guides and support staff
exclusions: Travel to and from the base point
Porter or mule charges for personal bags
essentials: Backpack, 40 to 50 L, with rain cover
Warm layers: fleece, down jacket, thermals
Cap or sun hat, gloves, sunglasses

slides.subtitle: Cedar forests and snow peaks on the horizon

reviews.name: Aarav Mehta
reviews.body: Well planned from start to finish. The guide kept a steady pace and checked on everyone along the way.

reviews.name: Neha Sharma
reviews.body: The trail was green and quiet, and the team handled the rain without any fuss. Great first Himalayan trek.

reviews.name: Rohan Verma
reviews.body: Tough climb, but the leaders explained each day clearly and the camps were warm and comfortable.

reviews.name: Priya Nair
reviews.body: Lovely group, great food at every stop, and a guide who knew every turn. Would trek with them again.

reviews.name: Karan Singh
reviews.body: Easy to book, easy to follow. The lake at sunrise made the whole trip worth it.

reviews.name: Ishita Roy
reviews.body: Eleven days felt short. Clear weather updates and kind, patient support from the whole team.

reviews.name: Vikram Rao
reviews.body: Every lake looked better than the last. The local crew looked after us very well.

reviews.name: Ananya Das
reviews.body: We took the kids on this one. The pace was gentle and the guides made it fun for them.

items.q: How do I choose the right trek?
items.a: Start with your fitness level and the number of days you have. For a first trek, pick an easy or easy-to-moderate route of 4 to 6 days with a gradual climb, and check the best season. If you are unsure, send us an enquiry and we will suggest options.

items.q: Can a beginner choose a tough trek?
items.a: We do not recommend it. High altitude, steep slopes and rough ground need experience and fitness. Begin with an easier trek and build up from there.

items.q: Is there an age limit?
items.a: There is no fixed age limit. Fitness and health matter more. If you have a medical condition, please check with your doctor before booking.

items.q: Can I join the trek solo?
items.a: Yes. Book a fixed-date batch and we will place you in a group with other trekkers.

items.q: What food will I get?
items.a: Simple, filling vegetarian meals and snacks on the trail. Tell us about allergies or special diets when you book so we can plan ahead.

items.q: How much water should I carry?
items.a: Carry two one-litre bottles. You can refill them at every camp.

items.q: How do I book a trek?
items.a: Pick a trek and a batch date, then send us an enquiry using the form below. We will confirm availability and share the payment steps.

items.q: What is included in the price?
items.a: Add your own inclusions here, for example camps or stays, meals on the trek, trek leader and guides, permits and a safety kit.

items.q: Can I change my batch date?
items.a: Add your date-change rules here. Ask us as early as possible so we can check space in other batches.

items.q: What is the cancellation policy?
items.a: Add your cancellation and refund terms here.

items.q: Can I trek with kids?
items.a: Yes, on easy routes such as Dayara Bugyal. Check the minimum age for each trek with our team before booking.

items.q: Can we book a private family batch?
items.a: Add your private or customised trek details here, including group size and pricing.

items.q: What should kids carry?
items.a: A small day pack with water, a snack and a rain layer. Adults or porters carry the main load.

items.q: What gear can I rent?
items.a: Jackets, trekking poles, sleeping bags and shoes. Add your full list here.

items.q: How does renting work?
items.a: Tell us the gear and dates in your enquiry. You collect and return it at the base point. Add your own steps here.

items.q: Is there a deposit?
items.a: Add your deposit and damage policy here.

items.q: What is the repeat trek policy?
items.a: Describe what you offer to returning trekkers here, for example a discount on the next booking.

items.q: How do I claim it?
items.a: Add the steps here, such as quoting your earlier booking ID.

items.q: What is a Trek Ambassador?
items.a: A past trekker who shares their experience and helps new trekkers choose and prepare. Describe your own programme here.
